inputs.original_text: An Indiana judge blocked a law restricting abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdened people’s ability to obtain abortions in line with their sincerely held religious beliefs. That matters: the state shouldn’t impose one religious or political view on everyone, especially when doing so limits people’s bodily autonomy and access to care. LifeNews.com’s “killing babies” framing turns a legal dispute over religious freedom into inflammatory rhetoric rather than engaging with the rights at stake.
inputs.modified_text: An Indiana judge blocked a law restricting abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdened people’s ability to follow their sincerely held religious beliefs. That’s a crucial check on state power: no government should impose one religious or political worldview by restricting people’s bodily autonomy and access to care. These restrictions fall hardest on people with the fewest resources and choices. LifeNews.com’s “killing babies” language is inflammatory framing, not a serious engagement with religious freedom or the real consequences of denying care.
